title: Website development for nonprofits | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs builds nonprofit websites with donation pages, volunteer sign-up, and event registration. Fixed-price projects quoted after a scoping call.
h1: Website and web application development for nonprofits
intro: A nonprofit website typically has to do several jobs at once: explain the mission and programs, take donations, register people for events, recruit volunteers, and post the annual report and Form 990 for anyone checking. Many organizations run a WordPress or Squarespace site with a donation form from Givebutter, Donorbox, or PayPal bolted on, an Eventbrite link for events, and a Google Form for volunteer interest, each holding its own copy of the contact list.

Creosote Labs builds websites and web applications for nonprofits that bring those pieces together. We build marketing sites with clear program pages and a direct way to give, and customer-facing tools such as donation flows, volunteer applications, event registration, and client intake forms that write to the organization's database instead of a separate inbox. Hosting setup, domain configuration, and handover with documentation are included.
projects: A program and mission website with a donation page that records each gift in the donor database.
A volunteer portal where applicants submit an application, pick shifts, and log hours.
An event registration tool that handles tickets, sponsorship tiers, and attendee lists for an annual gala.
A client intake form for a service program that replaces paper forms and feeds a case tracking system.
A public transparency page that hosts the annual report, audited financials, and Form 990 in one place.

faqs.q: How are nonprofit website projects priced?
faqs.a: Website and application projects are quoted after a scoping call at a fixed price, with no hourly billing. Hosting setup and domain configuration are part of the project.

faqs.q: Can the site connect to the donor database we already use?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Donation and sign-up forms can write to systems such as Bloomerang, Neon CRM, or Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, depending on what the platform supports. We confirm the specifics during scoping.

faqs.q: Who updates the site after launch?
faqs.a: Staff do. The site is built so that program pages, events, and news can be edited without a developer, and the handover includes written documentation for whoever maintains it.
